_meta.indication: Palynziq is indicated to reduce blood phenylalanine concentrations in adult patients with phenylketonuria (PKU) who have uncontrolled blood phenylalanine concentrations greater than 600 micromol/L on existing management.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (to two target maintenance doses), open-label induction/titration/maintenance regimen starting at 2.5 mg once weekly and titrating to a target dose of 20 mg or 40 mg once daily.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction of blood Phe concentrations from baseline.
pivotal_trials.result: Of 118 patients with baseline blood Phe > 600 micromol/L on the 20 mg once daily dose, 52% achieved a single blood Phe measurement of ≤ 600 micromol/L, and 30% achieved blood Phe ≤ 600 micromol/L for 16 consecutive weeks while in the open-label extension of Trial 165-302.

pivotal_trials.design: 8-week, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal design in enriched treatment responders, comparing continued pegvaliase (20 or 40 mg once daily) to matching placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult PKU patients who were treatment responders (≥ 20% reduction in blood Phe from pre-treatment baseline).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in blood Phe concentration from Part 2 Baseline to Part 2 Week 8.
pivotal_trials.n: 86 patients randomized in Part 2 (20 mg: N=29 vs placebo N=14; 40 mg: N=29 vs placebo N=14)
pivotal_trials.result: Both active arms maintained blood Phe significantly better than placebo (p<0.0001). Difference in LS mean change from Part 2 baseline to Week 8: -973.0 micromol/L (95% CI -1204.2, -741.9) for 20 mg/day vs placebo, and -588.5 micromol/L (95% CI -830.1, -346.9) for 40 mg/day vs placebo.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20% in either treatment phase): injection site reactions, arthralgia, hypersensitivity reactions, headache, generalized skin reactions lasting at least 14 days, pruritus, nausea, abdominal pain, oropharyngeal pain, vomiting, cough, diarrhea, and fatigue. Injection site reactions occurred in 88% (induction/titration) and arthralgia in 74%. The most serious risk is anaphylaxis; 31 (11%) of 285 patients discontinued due to adverse reactions.
target_moa: Pegvaliase is a phenylalanine-metabolizing enzyme (PEGylated recombinant phenylalanine ammonia lyase, rAvPAL) that substitutes for the deficient phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) enzyme in PKU by providing an alternate pathway for phenylalanine metabolism.
modality: Enzyme (PEGylated recombinant phenylalanine ammonia lyase); enzyme substitution therapy.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF ANAPHYLAXIS — Anaphylaxis has been reported after administration of Palynziq and may occur at any time during treatment. Administer the initial dose under supervision of a healthcare provider equipped to manage anaphylaxis and observe for at least 60 minutes; prescribe auto-injectable epinephrine to all patients. Because of the risk of anaphylaxis, Palynziq is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the Palynziq REMS.

rems.type: Palynziq is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the Palynziq REMS, because of the risk of anaphylaxis.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues.

summary.text: Palynziq (pegvaliase-pqpz) for adult PKU received Orphan Drug Designation (March 8, 1995) and Fast Track Designation (11/22/2011), and the BLA was granted priority review (PDUFA goal date initially February 28, 2018, extended to May 28, 2018 after a major amendment). It was not an accelerated approval and was not referred to an advisory committee.
